summary_en.motivation: To investigate the corrosion behavior of Al-12Si alloy produced by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Ultrafine-grained Al-12Si samples were fabricated via SLM and subjected to electrochemical corrosion tests.
summary_en.result: SLM-processed alloy exhibited improved corrosion resistance compared to conventionally cast counterpart.
summary_en.validation: Experimental corrosion testing (potentiodynamic polarization and immersion).

papers.title: Printability Study of Bioprinted Tubular Structures Using Liquid Hydrogel Precursors in a Support Bath
papers.abstract: Microextrusion-based bioprinting within a support bath material is an emerging additive manufacturing paradigm for complex three-dimensional (3D) tissue construct fabrication. Although a support bath medium enables arbitrary in-process geometries to be printed, a significant challenge lies in preserving the shape fidelity upon the extraction of the support bath material. Based on the bioprinting in a support bath paradigm, this paper advances quantitative analyses to systematically determine the printability of cell-laden liquid hydrogel precursors towards filament-based tissue constructs. First, a yield stress nanoclay material is judiciously selected as the support bath medium owing to its insensitivity to temperature and ionic variations that are considered in the context of the current gelatin-alginate bio-ink material formulation. Furthermore, phenomenological observations for the rheology-mediated print outcomes enable the compositions for the bio-ink material (10% gelatin, 3% alginate), in tandem with the support bath medium (4% nanoclay, 0.5% CaCl2), to be identified. To systematically evaluate the performance outcomes for bioprinting within a support bath, this paper advances an experimental parametric study to optimize the 3D structural shape fidelity by varying parameters such as the layer height, extrusion flowrate, printing temperature, and printhead speed, towards fabricating complex 3D structures with the stabilization of the desired shape outcome. Specifically, it is found that the layer height and printhead speed are determinant parameters for the extent of successive layer fusion. Moreover, maintenance of an optimal bath temperature is identified as a key parameter for establishing the printability for the hydrogel bio-ink. Studying this effect is enabled by the custom design of a PID temperature control system with integration with the bioprinter for real-time precision control of the support bath temperature. In order to qualify the printed construct, a surface irregularity metric, defined as the average height difference between consecutive local maximum and minimum points of the binary image contour for the printed structure, is advanced to evaluate the quality of the printed constructs. Complex one-to-four bifurcating tubular structure prints demonstrate the applicability of the optimized bioprinting parameter space to create exemplar 3D human vessel-like structures. Finally, a cell viability assay and perfusion test for a printed cell-laden tubular element demonstrates high cell survival rates and leakage-free flow, respectively.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究支撑浴中液态水凝胶前体的可打印性。
summary_zh.method: 通过实验参数研究优化打印条件。
summary_zh.result: 确定了层高和打印速度等关键参数。
summary_zh.validation: 通过细胞活力和灌注测试验证。

summary_en.motivation: This work aims to quantify the printability of cell-laden liquid hydrogel precursors within a support bath for fabricating complex 3D tissue constructs.
summary_en.method: Systematic experimental parametric optimization was conducted, along with PID temperature control, to achieve high shape fidelity.
summary_en.result: Layer height and printhead speed were found to be critical for layer fusion, and optimal bath temperature was identified as key for printability.
summary_en.validation: Biological and functional validation were performed via cell viability assay and perfusion test on printed tubular structures.
